name: Percentage Change, Two Periods
description: Calculate the overall percentage change after a value moves through two consecutive periods of change.
formula: Final value = Start value × (1 + Rate period 1) × (1 + Rate period 2); Overall % change = (Final value − Start value) / Start value × 100
business_contexts: a retailer whose sales rose one quarter and fell the next
a company whose costs rose two years running at different rates
an investment that gained one year and lost the next
a market that grew in one period and contracted in the next
a subscription base that grew one month and shrank the next
question_patterns: Given the starting value and the two period-over-period rates below, what is the overall percentage change?
Calculate the overall percentage change after both periods of change shown below.
What is the combined percentage change across the two periods given?
Applying both rates in sequence to the starting value below, what is the total percentage change?
Calculate the net percentage change after the value moves through both periods shown.
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate final value = start_value × (1 + rate_period1) × (1 + rate_period2)
Step 2: Calculate overall percentage change = (final_value − start_value) / start_value × 100
key_insight: Two sequential percentage changes don't add — they compound. A 10% rise followed by a 10% fall does not return you to where you started.
common_mistakes: Adding the two rates together instead of applying them sequentially
Applying both rates to the original start value instead of applying the second rate to the already-changed value
framework_soundbite: Sequential percentages multiply, they don't add — chain the multipliers, not the rates.
